solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Upright piano in bash: tuning note ruined

parts.note: have a bash = have a go
orchestras tune to the A
all is lost = ruined
p = piano (soft) in music; it sits inside LOST: L(P)OST

explanation.surface: A musical party where the piano is hopelessly out of tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants 'upright piano' as one instrument; 'Upright' alone is the definition, a goalpost being an upright.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalpost is one of the two uprights of a goal.

clue.text: Understand individual has secured manuscript, a precious item

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast

parts.note: 'I get it' = I understand
standard abbreviation, held inside GET: GE(MS)T
one = a single individual

explanation.surface: Someone realises a lone person has got hold of a valuable old manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has secured' is the container signal, but it belongs to 'Understand', not to 'individual' next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A general description: a cut jewel is one example of a precious item.

clue.text: Brightest star heads for home abruptly after a recording

indicators.note: take the first letter of each following word

parts.note: as printed
LP = long-playing record
first letters of home and abruptly

explanation.surface: A pop star rushes home the moment a recording session ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'star' is a celebrity; the definition means the astronomical one. Alpha is the name given to the brightest star in a constellation, as in Alpha Centauri.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomer's naming convention: stars in each constellation take Greek letters in order of brightness, so the first letter labels the brightest.

clue.text: Public meeting to urge diet?

parts.note: press = urge, as in pressing someone to act
a diet is a formal assembly, as in the Diet of Worms

explanation.surface: A gathering held to encourage people to slim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diet' wants to be about food; here it is the old word for a legislative assembly or conference. The question mark flags that twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A press conference is a meeting held publicly for journalists.

clue.text: Foolish person in school mess

parts.note: sch. is the abbreviation for school
muck = mess, dirt

explanation.surface: An idiot lands in trouble at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal but is only a link: the foolish person is found in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmuck is Yiddish-derived slang for a fool.

clue.text: Fight doctor in film

indicators.note: the doctor is placed in the film, so his letters sit inside it

parts.note: a film of paint is a coat
MB = Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree; it goes between CO and AT

explanation.surface: A brawl involving a doctor in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' reads as a movie; it is a thin layer, a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat means fight, as noun or verb.

clue.text: I will avoid describing original server as excellent

parts.note: of can mean concerning or describing, as in a story of love

indicators.note: to avoid is to keep out, so the letter named is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: the first waiter, playfully, is the original person who served

explanation.surface: A modest speaker declining to praise the first tennis server as excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I will avoid' drops I from THE FIRST WAITER to leave THE FIRST WATER; the server is a waiter, not a tennis player.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the first water is an idiom from grading diamonds, meaning of the highest quality.

clue.text: Lives in this place will retain power where life exists

parts.note: bios = biographies, lives
here = in this place
P = power in physics, kept between the other two pieces

explanation.surface: Life stories kept in one place still have influence where people live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lives' reads as a verb; here it is the plural noun, biographies.
explanation.definitionFit: The biosphere is the part of the Earth where living things exist.

clue.text: Saunter to end of road and do nothing after one leaves

indicators.note: after places the shortened idle word following the earlier pieces
the end of a word is its last letter
the numeral goes away from the word for doing nothing, so it is dropped

parts.note: to idle is to do nothing
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lazy stroll to the end of the road and then lazing about once a companion has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To toddle is to walk in a slow, unhurried way, a gentle saunter.

clue.text: People attending American University fancy food at the Sorbonne?

parts.note: the gate is the number of spectators at an event
initials

explanation.surface: Students at an American college hanker after the fine food served at a Paris university.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sorbonne is a Paris university, signalling a French word; gâteau is French for cake. 'Fancy' is an adjective here, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich, elaborate cake: fancy food, and French.

clue.text: Chap hogging last of syrup — from this?

definitions.note: the definition points back to syrup: the tree that syrup comes from

parts.note: a chap is a male

indicators.note: take the last letter of syrup

parts.note: last letter of syrup, held in the middle of the chap

explanation.surface: A man greedily keeping the last of the syrup to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'from this?', i.e. the source of syrup, which is the maple tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Maple syrup is made from the sap of the maple tree.

clue.text: Hard material — too hard, we fancy

indicators.note: fancy as a verb: let the letters be imagined in a new arrangement

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Someone complains a material is too tough for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard' appears in both definition and fodder; only the second is letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartwood is the dense, hard inner wood of a tree trunk.

clue.text: Schools silent after dismissing current change

indicators.note: silent comes after the shortened schools word
dismissing sends away, so the symbol for current is removed from the word

parts.note: to train is to school, teach
I is the physics symbol for electric current
mute means silent

explanation.surface: School classes fall quiet once the current lesson is let out, bringing a change.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmute is to change one thing into another, as alchemists hoped to change lead into gold.

clue.text: Get rid of devious character seen around Times page

indicators.note: the eel is placed around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: an eel is a slippery, devious person
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A shifty figure lurking around the newspaper's pages needs to be thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but it is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to force someone out, to get rid of them.

clue.text: Clear with agreement to adopt Republican broadcasting company

parts.note: to clear a profit is to net it
w = with

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in as one's own, so the agreement takes the Republican into itself

parts.note: OK = agreement
R = Republican; O(R)K

explanation.surface: A TV channel cleared to take on a Republican by agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' means to make as profit, net.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcasting sense: a chain of linked stations, as with the big American TV networks.

clue.text: Pursue clubs, perhaps, for training gear

parts.note: track = follow, pursue
clubs is one example of a suit in cards

explanation.surface: Chasing golf clubs to use in practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' suggests golf; it is the card suit, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example of a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by use: the loose top and trousers athletes wear to warm up and train.

clue.text: One not quoted abandoning chapter

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so the chapter abbreviation is dropped

parts.note: uncited means not quoted as a source

explanation.surface: Someone not mentioned in a book drops out of a chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: One can mean joined together as a single whole, as in 'we are one', which is united.

clue.text: Working to death, working without hint of alleviation? Exactly

parts.note: on means working, operating, as a machine is on

indicators.note: working here means being worked over into a new arrangement
without means lacking, so the letter is removed
a hint of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone toiling relentlessly with no relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without hint of alleviation' takes A from TO DEATH, and 'working' rearranges what is left, TODETH, into THEDOT.
explanation.definitionFit: On the dot is an idiom meaning precisely on time, exactly.

clue.text: Fussed vaguely, satisfied to be welcoming a couple of females

indicators.note: a host welcoming guests takes them inside

parts.note: fed = satisfied (with food)
A plus two Fs, f being the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A well-fed host dithering over the arrival of two women guests.
explanation.walkthrough: To faff about is British slang for fussing around without achieving much.
explanation.definitionFit: Faffed means fussed ineffectually, dithered.

clue.text: Welshman, finally losing heart, accommodated by father and daughter

indicators.note: to be accommodated is to be given lodging, so the remnant is housed inside the father

parts.note: dad = father
FINALLY without its inner letters; DA(FY)D
d = daughter

explanation.surface: A Welshman who eventually lost his nerve, taken in by his family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' is the fodder here, not an adverb. Dafydd is the Welsh form of David.
explanation.definitionFit: Dafydd is a typical Welsh man's name, standing for any Welshman.

clue.text: Advertisement possibly attached to new gate

parts.note: a poster is one kind of advertisement
n = new

explanation.surface: An ad stuck onto a freshly built gate.
explanation.walkthrough: A postern is a back or side gate, especially in a castle wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific kind: the small back or side gate in a castle or city wall.

clue.text: Mate shipping oars, drifting in shade

indicators.note: to ship oars is to bring them aboard, so the mate takes the letters inside

parts.note: pal is informal for mate, friend

indicators.note: drifting means moving aimlessly, so the letters of oars wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A boat crew member pulls in the oars and drifts along in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a light umbrella that gives shade from the sun.

clue.text: Rubbish suggestion mostly thrown up in computer program

indicators.note: in a down clue, thrown up means turned upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an idea is a suggestion

explanation.surface: A poor suggestion was mostly rejected within a software project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts IDEA to IDE; ROT then IDE, read upwards, gives EDITOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a program for writing and changing text or code on a computer.

clue.text: Dark changes enveloping area in African city

indicators.note: the rearranged DARK wraps around A
DARK's letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram of DARK
a = area, enveloped by the shuffled DARK

explanation.surface: A gloomy change coming over part of an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: Dakar is the capital of Senegal.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the capital of Senegal, on the westernmost point of mainland Africa.

clue.text: Texas city accommodating couples runs this? Not half

parts.note: a table for two accommodates a couple
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: not half means half of the word is dropped, so only its first two letters stay

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a Texan city hosting couples is organised like this.
explanation.definitionFit: Fort Worth is a large city in Texas, next to Dallas.

clue.text: Novel of Paris and of another city

definitions.meaning: the French word for a novel: 'of Paris' means in French
the adjective for the Italian capital

explanation.surface: A book about Paris and another city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of Paris' means in French, not set in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman is the French word for a novel, and also means of Rome.

clue.text: Rippling nude torso — beefy stuff

indicators.note: the letters move like rippling muscles into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A muscular bare chest, the very picture of beefiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beefy' seems to describe the torso; it is literal: tournedos are beef steaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tournedos are small round steaks cut from beef fillet.

clue.text: Returned lots of cotton — it's shrinking

indicators.note: the letters run backwards
lots of something is a large part of it rather than the whole, so the fabric loses its final letter

parts.note: DIMITY is a cotton fabric; drop its last letter

explanation.surface: Cotton sent back because it shrinks in the wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrinking' suggests laundry; it means shy, as in a shrinking violet. Dimity is a light striped cotton.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrinking means timid, shying away.

clue.text: Excessive energy in sailors is not good

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the sailors' abbreviation

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's sailors
OTT, over the top, means excessive
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Too much enthusiasm among the crew is frowned upon.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten means bad, of poor quality, the opposite of good.

clue.text: Wind player at home tucking into wine

indicators.note: to tuck into something is to get stuck inside it, so these letters go into the wine

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
in = at home, placed inside the wine

explanation.surface: A flatulent musician staying home to drink wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind player' reads as a musician; the definition is the instrument that plays wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a woodwind instrument, a player of wind in a sense.
